# Skill Learning and Composition

[Home](../../../../README.md) · [All categories](../../../README.md) · [简体中文](skill-composition_cn.md)

Manipulation Action Models → Multi-Fingered Dexterous Hand Manipulation Research → Robot Manipulation Policies and Control → Skill Learning and Composition

Learn reusable skills, skill structure, inter-skill transitions and sequential composition. Record how the skill order is obtained, how transitions depend on the next skill, and how completion triggers switching. Executing a given sequence does not establish autonomous task planning or generalization to unseen orders; human-video learning remains a method tag.

| [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.SKILL.1] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-skill-1"></a> | **DexStitch｜Human-video transfer · Contact-aware conversion · Skill transitions and composition**<br>[DexStitch: Learning and Composing Dexterous Skills from Human Videos via Contact-Aware Robotic Inpainting](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.17789v1)<br>Byeonggyeol Choi, Seongmin Jung, Unghui Nam, Youngbo Song, Sunhong Min, MinHyung Lee, Byonghyo Shim, Yongseok Lee<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `human-video` `egocentric-video` `video-to-robot` `skill-learning` `skill-composition` `transition-skill` `next-skill-conditioning` `closed-loop-skill-switching` `contact-aware-retargeting` `robotic-inpainting` `demonstration-synthesis` `diffusion-policy` `imitation-learning` `real-world` | DexStitch extracts manipulation skills and transition demonstrations from human videos, trains a shared diffusion policy through contact-aware human-to-robot conversion, conditions connecting motions on the current and next skills, and predicts skill progression for closed-loop switching through a given sequence.<br>**Evaluation scope:** RGB-estimated finger contacts guide both retargeting and finger/object occlusion in synthetic frames. Pretraining uses about 240 converted long-horizon human episodes; mixed fine-tuning adds about 32 single-skill robot demonstrations. Transitions are supervised only by human video. A video classifier or script supplies the order; the shared policy predicts actions and skill progression rather than autonomously planning tasks. Hardware is an RB5-850E arm with xHand, executing 6 arm and 12 hand joint commands. Four skills receive five isolated trials each, averaging 80% success. The 77.5% sequence metric averages 40 skill executions across ten fixed four-skill rollouts, not fully successful sequence rollouts. Unseen orderings are untested. Compositing assumes wrap grasps with the thumb in front and other contacting fingers behind the object. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.17789v1) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.SKILL.2] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-skill-2"></a> | **DexCompose｜Skill composition · Finger action ownership · Residual RL**<br>[DexCompose: Reusing Dexterous Policies for Multi-Task Manipulation with a Single Hand](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.28323v1)<br>Dihong Huang, Zhenyu Wei, Zhuxiu Xu, Yunchao Yao, Sikai Li, Mingyu Ding<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `skill-composition` `pretrained-policy-reuse` `finger-action-ownership` `action-masking` `release-test` [residual-rl](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [ppo](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `diffusion-policy` `imitation-learning` `agent` `llm-finger-allocation` `grasp-preservation` `shadow-hand` `simulation` | DexCompose selects finger ownership through release tests and an LLM, keeps pretrained skill policies frozen, and learns two PPO residuals for grasp preservation and downstream-action adaptation; masked action assembly lets one hand retain an object while performing another interaction.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Each primitive diffusion policy learns from 50 demonstrations, reads two low-dimensional proprioceptive/task-geometric observations and predicts 32 steps of 28-D Floating Shadow Hand commands (6 wrist plus 22 finger targets). After A succeeds, its grasp configuration is stored. Release tests measure retention and clean disengagement; an LLM Agent selects a fixed mask per task pair before execution, not stepwise actions. Preserved fingers receive the stored reference plus an A residual; the wrist and released fingers receive frozen B-policy actions plus a B residual. Both residuals are PPO-trained MLPs: A uses object/finger/contact state, while B additionally reads nominal actions and the mask. A stabilizers are first learned per retention skill; B residuals still require pair-specific training, optionally fine-tuning the A residual at a lower rate. Base policies stay frozen; the full method is not training-free composition. Isaac Lab combines four retention skills (GraspBall, PourMug, PickCan, PickStick) with door opening, button pressing, microwave opening and switch actuation into 16 pairs, evaluated with 32 rollouts across eight seeds per pair. Continuous A retention and B completion are both required: mean success is 77.43%, falling to 9.13% without the A residual. Validation covers single-hand simulation and two-skill compositions, without reported hardware tests. Training/evaluation code is public; data and checkpoint downloads remain unverified. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.28323v1) · [Project](https://devon018.github.io/DexCompose-Webpage/) · [Code](https://github.com/Devon018/DexCompose) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-27 |
